prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for ICICIBANK (base year 2022):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2022,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 119500,
      "net_income_cr": 31500,
      "eps": 45.2
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 138500,
      "net_income_cr": 38500,
      "eps": 55.1
    },
    {
      "year": 2025,
      "revenue_cr": 159000,
      "net_income_cr": 46500,
      "eps": 66.5
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Loan book continues to grow at ~18-20% annually driven by retail credit expansion, improving asset quality (Gross NPA fell from 5.33% to 3.76%), and rising NIM (3.96% in FY22 vs 3.69% in FY21), supporting Total Income growth of ~15-17% per year.",
    "Net profit margin expansion continues as provisions normalize post-COVID (provisions-to-core-operating-profit fell from 36.57% to 22.53%), with credit costs declining further and operating leverage improving, enabling PAT growth of ~20-22% annually."
  ],
  "reasoning": "This is ICICI Bank, so Total Income (Interest Earned + Other Income) is used as the Revenue line. FY2022 standalone Total Income is approximately \u20b9104,892 crore (\u20b91,048,920.8 million) and net profit is \u20b923,339 crore (\u20b9233,394.9 million standalone); consolidated revenue from geographical segments is \u20b9158,291 crore (\u20b91,582,907.5 million) but standalone figures are used for consistency with the primary P&L. An anomaly is flagged because FY2021 and FY2022 were distorted by COVID-related provisions (\u20b947.5 billion extra in FY21) and subsequent sharp provision releases, making year-on-year PAT growth of ~44% non-representative of a sustainable run-rate. The 3-5 year CAGR for Total Income is estimated at ~12-14% (interest income grew 9.2% in FY22 over FY21, but loan book grew 13.5% on average assets and NIM expanded), while PAT trajectory benefits from mean-reversion of credit costs. Projections blend a ~15-16% revenue CAGR (reflecting strong retail loan growth, NIM at ~4%+, and rising fee income from subsidiaries/ecosystem) with ~20% PAT CAGR as provisions normalise, balance sheet remains well-capitalised (RoE improved to 14.77%, RoA to 1.84%), and management's guidance on digital-led retail expansion and MSME/SME segments provides upside; EPS is projected on approximately 698 crore shares outstanding with modest dilution from ESOPs."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

RESPONSE FORMAT: Begin your response DIRECTLY with the opening brace { — no reasoning or text before the JSON.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
